title: AI and human behavior
asks: How do people trust, rely on and work with AI, and what should a product or policy do about it?
lead: Medical-AI trust experiments, generative AI collaboration studies, the cloud-hosted AI task I built, and honest null results.

rows.field: Human-AI decision processes; calibrated trust; over-trust
rows.mine: Six preregistered experiments on trust in doctors versus medical AI, using Weight-on-Advice to measure reliance. More than 3,000 participants recruited.
Two preregistered experiments (N = 1,299) on drafting versus editing with generative AI: quality, time, ownership and engagement.

rows.field: Prototype research tools; interfacing with models
rows.mine: A participant-facing task on the ChatGPT API, hosted on AWS, with random assignment in Qualtrics.
Master's thesis (N = 305): people obeyed computer and human instructors about equally.
NIH protocol on how people read genomic risk when a geneticist or an AI reviews the result. I am the lead researcher under the principal investigator. It is in ethics review and has no data yet.

limits: I study people's responses to AI. I have not done AI safety engineering, red-teaming, model evaluation building or machine-learning engineering.

title: Experimentation and product research
asks: What did the change do to behavior, and what should we build or measure next?
lead: Randomized experiments, power planning, quasi-experimental causal inference, dashboards and mixed methods.

rows.field: Design and run experiments; rigorous, trustworthy experiments
rows.mine: Randomized, preregistered experiments in my thesis, dissertation and generative AI studies. I call them randomized controlled experiments, not platform A/B tests.

rows.field: Power; minimum detectable effect; sample-size planning
rows.mine: Power planning and sensitivity analysis in the thesis, dissertation and mega-analysis.

rows.field: Causal inference when randomization is unavailable
rows.mine: Difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity and propensity-score matching on more than 100,000 student records.
Multilevel, moderation and causal-mediation models, with a specification curve and multiple-comparison corrections.
Tableau dashboards used by department chairs and administrators.
Focus groups, surveys, interviews and daily diary studies.

limits: I have no A/B platform, log-data or product-analytics experience. SQL is still developing.

title: Survey science and measurement
asks: Is the measure valid and reliable, and is the survey good enough to trust?
lead: Instrument development, structural equation modeling, panel quality and longitudinal measurement.

rows.mine: Trust, reasoning and mind-perception measures built for the dissertation, and a smartphone self-inclusion scale (in preparation, first author).
Factor and path models in graduate coursework and a data competition, and Mplus models in the dissertation.
Reliability and validity reporting for a published gaming-motivation scale and a VR symptom questionnaire, where I was a contributor.

rows.field: Online survey panel vendors; fitness for use
rows.mine: Prolific, CloudResearch, MTurk and university pools, with attention checks and exclusions.
Daily diary studies, a 15-day behavior study and an eight-week field study.

limits: I have no item response theory, test equating, survey weighting or probability-panel experience.

title: Behavioral and applied research
asks: Why do people think, decide, trust or act this way, and what should we test?
lead: Experiments, theory, interventions, mixed methods and decision-ready findings.

rows.mine: Theory for Risk Creep, the parasocial identification paper, the smartphone wellbeing review and my dissertation.
The master's thesis and six-study dissertation, from question through design, recruitment, analysis and writing.
A 15-day digital-health study with daily diary reports and a seven-day adherence follow-up.
Experiments, surveys, focus groups and administrative data, used together.
Preregistration, public materials and Quarto reports.

limits: My experience is academic and applied research. I have not held a long industry UX role or owned a product.

title: Health and digital health research
asks: What affects patient behavior, experience, adherence and trust?
lead: NIH work, clinical-study administration, medical AI, health behavior and longitudinal measurement.

rows.mine: Health beliefs, genetic-risk interpretation and trust in medical AI, in the dissertation and NIH projects.
The 15-day dissertation study, which found no reliable intervention effect.

rows.field: Regulated study operations; clinical recruitment support
rows.mine: Recruitment administration for an NIH clinical trial.
First-author secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial of a ghrelin-receptor blocker (published 2026).
A virtual-patient project on how race and weight cues shape the reading of genetic risk (N = 200).

limits: I am not a clinician and have no payer, claims or electronic-health-record experience. I do not claim health-economics expertise.

title: Research programs and operations
asks: Can this person keep a complex research enterprise moving?
lead: Portfolio ownership, people coordination, governance, timelines, recruitment and process.

rows.field: Manage a research portfolio; prioritize concurrent workstreams
rows.mine: Six to seven concurrent projects at Georgetown with a student team, and six NIH projects now.
Research assistant supervision since 2017, with teams of up to 15.

rows.field: Manage approvals, protocols and compliant operations
rows.mine: IRB protocols written and managed at two universities.
Redesigned the Georgetown participant pool; research yield reportedly rose 50% the next year.

rows.field: Develop proposals, budgets and delivery plans
rows.mine: Three named grants and fellowships, plus budgets and timelines for the dissertation.

limits: My evidence is small-team and portfolio leadership. I have not directed a large organization or served as principal investigator on major funding.

rows.field: Evaluation design; implementation and outcome evaluation
rows.mine: An evaluation of a university summer-skills program with focus groups, surveys and student outcomes.
Matching, regression discontinuity and difference-in-differences on administrative records.
Recurring dashboards and reports for chairs and administrators.
Evidence work behind the Georgetown GRE-optional decision, and a gender identity and pronoun data policy that was adopted.

limits: I have not done community-based evaluation. I describe recommendations as delivered, and name the decision only when someone acted on it.

Surveys, focus groups, experiments and longitudinal data in one question.
Regression, multilevel and moderation models.
Learner outcomes work, a guest lecture on people analytics, and a university summer-skills program evaluation.

Workshops on power analysis, R and open science, and R and Quarto at NIH.
A 100-point course design with weekly writing, a self-evaluation and a staged final project.

rows.mine: Online-panel surveys, including a COVID-19 study with 569 completers.
More than 100,000 student records with reports and dashboards.
Applied in institutional research, and taught in a graduate evaluation course.
Policy memos, a Congressional-testimony project and a policy poster in graduate work.
The gender identity and pronoun data task force.

rows.mine: Trust in medical AI, the generative AI collaboration experiments, and current NIH work on AI-generated health information.
First author of the eight-experiment mega-analysis and of the published crossover-trial analysis. Co-first author of the generative AI paper (under review).
Psychology of Technology at Georgetown, plus recitation, lead teaching fellow and guest lecture roles.
An honors thesis, a conference graduate mentorship and a former student's accepted conference project.
Three small and internal awards.

The obedience thesis and the dissertation on trust in medical AI.
Recruited more than 3,000 participants with attention-check and exclusion screening.
Video and media coding and transcription in earlier lab roles.

More than 100,000 student records, and a mega-analysis where I removed 173 placeholder rows.
Tableau dashboards for administrators, and Quarto reports.

rows.mine: The dissertation and graduate project work, framed from question to recommendation.
